title: NARROWNECK REEF
what_it_shows: Interview-style documentary with the reef's design engineer explaining why Narrowneck Reef was built (Northern Gold Coast Beach Protection Strategy, 1999), how the geotextile sandbags were placed by split-hull dredge, why a submerged reef beat groynes/beach dewatering as the chosen solution, and the marine growth/monitoring outcomes over ~10 years.
key_quotes: [00:00:19] "The [Narrowneck] Reef is a geotextile bag reef and its primary objective was Coastal protection."

[00:01:00] "...what we wanted was another control point just this side of Surfers Paradise we looked at groins we looked at beach dewatering... and the one that came out best was a submerged artificial Reef without the added bonuses of Surfing and Diving it was clearly the best solution."
[00:01:33] "We've constructed a structure that you can't see but it's constantly reducing the sand transport and the storm cut so we have a wider Beach a more stable Beach."
[00:01:57] "McQuade won the contract for dropping the sandbags he had bought in a split Hull Hopper barge that he developed specifically for doing this type of work."

[00:02:52] "The difference between a geotextile structure and a concrete or rock structure is the type of growth we get... 10 m of water we're getting Kelps we're getting Turtles and I've dive with dolphins."

[00:03:32] "The data that's been collected over the last 10 years from video cameras and other measurements... clearly show that it's been a highly successful device or structure for maintaining the health of the beach."
notes: Transcript pulled via yt-dlp --write-subs/--write-auto-subs (English captions available, dedupe-cleaned VTT). No frames extracted — video is narration/interview over B-roll and construction/marine footage rather than a single held shot depicting reef geometry; captioned with timestamps instead per Lior's short-video/embed preference.
